name: proxychains4
one_line: force any TCP program through a proxy (SOCKS or HTTP)
plain: `proxychains4` (also called proxychains) wraps another command so that its TCP connections go through one or more proxies you list in a config file. The program does not need to know about proxies: proxychains intercepts its network calls.
In security work it pairs with a SOCKS tunnel (chisel, `ssh -D`) so you can run nmap, curl, smbclient or other tools against an internal network that you reach only through a foothold.
when: Use ordinary tools against an internal network through a pivot.
Send traffic through Tor or a chain of proxies.
Test what a program does when it has to go through a proxy.

examples.title: Basic use
examples.explain: Runs curl, but its connection goes through the proxy named in the config.

examples.title: Quiet output
examples.explain: -q hides the [proxychains] lines. nmap must use -sT (TCP connect) and -Pn (no ping): SOCKS carries only TCP connections.

examples.title: Set up the proxy
examples.cmd:
sudo nano /etc/proxychains4.conf
# at the bottom, in [ProxyList]:
socks5 127.0.0.1 1080
examples.explain: Add the proxy at the end of the file. 1080 is where chisel R:socks and ssh -D listen by default.

examples.title: Use your own config file
examples.explain: -f points to a config for this one job instead of the system file.

examples.title: DNS through the proxy
examples.explain: Makes name lookups also go through the proxy so internal names resolve and nothing leaks to your own DNS.

examples.title: A whole shell through the proxy
examples.explain: Every program started from that shell is wrapped (works for dynamically linked programs).

options.plain: A proxy line. Types: socks5, socks4, http.

mistakes: Running nmap with the default SYN scan or with ping: it silently fails. Use -sT -Pn.
Forgetting to start the tunnel first (the connection is refused on 127.0.0.1:1080).
Trying to proxy UDP or ICMP: only TCP works.
Static binaries and some Go programs ignore proxychains because they do not use the system libraries.
try: Start `ssh -D 1080 user@host` to a lab machine and curl an internal page through proxychains.
Pair it with a chisel R:socks tunnel and scan a lab subnet.
Compare a scan with and without proxy_dns.
see_also: chisel(1), ssh(1) (-D), tor(1), nmap(1), socat(1), curl(1). The command is also installed as `proxychains`.
